A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

beryllum is a powerful tool for the understanding of the formation of the oldest stellar generations in the Galaxy, but it cannot be used to constrain the formation time of a globular cluster without additional constraints.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the study of light element abundances in globular cluster turnoff stars can provide important constraints on the formation and evolution of the first stars and the first generation of globular clusters in the Universe.
beryllum, together with lithium, can be a powerful probe of the first stars and their nucleosynthetic products, and of the first stellar generations in the Galaxy.
the study of beryllum is an important tool for the investigation of globular clusters and their formation, and should be pursued with the best quality spectra.
